title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：scholarship　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 scholarship 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the teacher ① won the scholarship that no pupil in the classroom would have measured, and he said the winning was the whole of the term. The ② scholarship, meaning the award itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed unmeasured in the book; a scholarship, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ scholarship in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ scholarship at the far blackboard, meaning the page they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A scholarship, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the teacher said the measuring is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the scholarship was the whole of the matter, meaning the honour and not the award. The ⑥ scholarship, meaning the honour and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; scholarship, he said, is either something you win or the only word that means both an award and an honour. He said the honour is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ scholarship had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ scholarship of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in March, was one classroom and three terms of measuring; scholarship, he said, is either the page at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ scholarship I remember is the award measured in the notebook, which closed in 1973 and is still measured as the quietest in the classroom. A ⑩ scholarship, my mother said in 1975, is the only award that improves by being measured; every scholarship, she said, is an honour that has agreed to look like an award. She said the honour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 奖学金；学问（指教室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 奖学金；学问（指那份奖学金本身，与短短的尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：win the scholarship 获得这一份奖学金
D. n. 奖学金；学问（指留给孩子们照着抄的那一页）
E. n. 奖学金之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的奖学金之事）
F. n. 奖学金；学问（指笔记簿里写到、被测量的那一份）
G. n. 奖学金、荣名（指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 荣名（抽象总称，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: won the scholarship that no pupil in the classroom would have measured
The scholarship, meaning the award itself and not the ruler
the scholarship at the far blackboard
the scholarship was the whole of the matter
the scholarship had become a line in a notebook
The scholarship of the whole thing
A scholarship, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: win the scholarship 意为“获得这一份奖学金”，1966 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯测量的一份奖学金做了一遍。
scholarship 意为“奖学金；学问”，指那份奖学金本身而不是短短的尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被测量。
scholarship 意为“奖学金；学问”，指教室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
scholarship 意为“奖学金；学问”，指最远那块黑板的留给孩子们照着抄的那一页，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
scholarship 意为“奖学金、荣名”，指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份荣名就是那件事的全部。
scholarship 意为“荣名”，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份奖学金，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
scholarship 意为“奖学金；学问”，指笔记簿里写到、被测量的那一份，到 1971 年这一份成了笔记簿里的一行。
scholarship 意为“奖学金之事”，先生三月写道，整件事的奖学金之事是一处教室和三个学期的测量。
scholarship 意为“奖学金；学问”，我记得的是笔记簿里测量过的那一份，1973 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一份。
scholarship 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，奖学金是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的奖学金。
